title: The Undertaker
summary:
This document is a comprehensive biographical article about Mark William Calaway, better known by his ring name The Undertaker, the legendary American retired professional wrestler. The article begins with an overview of his career, noting his 30-year tenure with WWE, his iconic "Deadman" persona, his record-setting 21 consecutive WrestleMania victories known as "The Streak," and his seven world championships, before detailing his 2022 WWE Hall of Fame induction.

The document covers his early life in Houston, Texas, including his education and basketball background before pursuing wrestling. His professional wrestling career is extensively chronicled in chronological sections, beginning with his early career (1987–1989) in World Class Championship Wrestling under various gimmicks such as "Texas Red," "The Master of Pain," and "The Punisher," followed by his brief stint in World Championship Wrestling (1989–1990) as "Mean Mark" Callous.

The bulk of the document details his WWE career (1990–2020), including the debut of the Undertaker character, his first WWF Championship win, the beginning of The Streak at WrestleMania VII, and the evolution of his character through multiple incarnations: the Rebirthed Deadman, Lord of Darkness, Ministry of Darkness, American Badass biker persona, Big Evil, the Return of the Deadman, and later championship reigns. Major storylines are covered in depth, including his feuds with Mankind (notably the famous Hell in a Cell match at King of the Ring 1998), the introduction of his storyline half-brother Kane as the Brothers of Destruction, the Broken Streak at the hands of Brock Lesnar at WrestleMania XXX, acclaimed matches against Shawn Michaels and Triple H, his final match against AJ Styles in the Boneyard match at WrestleMania 36, his retirement in 2020, and Hall of Fame induction in 2022, along with sporadic appearances and backstage roles through 2025.

Additional sections cover his legacy and critical reception (including recognition as one of wrestling's greatest performers alongside criticism of his later career), his personal life (three marriages, his Bone Street Krew backstage group, Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt, real estate investments, and political affiliations), his appearances in other media (acting roles, his "Six Feet Under" podcast, and WWE LFG), video game appearances, and an extensive list of championships and accomplishments including multiple Slammy Awards, Wrestling Observer Newsletter honors, and records for career victories.
